cards.text: Grab your apron, friend: we're in First John, a letter from John, who says he heard and saw Jesus with his own eyes (1 John 1:1). He's going back to basics, the message his readers have heard from the very beginning. Not new, not trendy, this recipe is OLDER than my mustache, and friend, this mustache has SEEN things.

cards.question: What's the message John's readers have heard from the beginning?

cards.text: John says don't be like Cain, Adam and Eve's son (Genesis 4:1), who belonged to the evil one and murdered his brother. Then John asks the big question himself: why'd Cain do it?

cards.question: John says Cain killed his brother because Cain's own deeds were ___, while his brother's deeds were ___.

cards.text: Then John turns to his readers and calls them brothers. He gives them a heads-up about how the world might treat them.

cards.question: True or false: John tells his brothers they should expect the world to love them.

cards.text: John says believers know they've passed from death to life. And he tells them EXACTLY how they know it.

cards.question: John says we know we've passed from death to life because we ___ our brothers.
True or false: John says the one who does not love remains in death.

cards.text: Then John talks about anyone who hates his brother. He's got a name for that person, and friend, it is NOT going on a cute little name tag.

cards.question: What does John call everyone who hates his brother?

cards.text: And John says you know eternal life does not reside in a murderer. No sprinkles, no peppermint, no little bow on the box, friend, John just pulled that one out of the oven and handed it to you HOT.
So what does real love actually look like? John says we can know it, and he points straight to Jesus.

cards.question: How does John say we know what love is?

answers.text: Jesus laid down His life for us
Jesus wrote it on stone tablets
Jesus showed it to us in a vision

cards.question: True or false: John says only Jesus was meant to lay down His life for others.

cards.text: Then John gets practical: picture someone with earthly possessions who sees his brother in need and withholds his compassion. That's me with a FULL cookie box, watching my friend go without, slowly closing the lid while we make eye contact.

cards.question: John asks a question about the person who sees his brother in need and won't show compassion. What does he ask?

answers.text: How can God's love abide in him
Why didn't his brother ask sooner
Who will pay his brother back

cards.text: Now John calls his readers little children and boils this whole thing down to one line about how love should show up.

cards.question: How does John tell his little children to love?

cards.text: Love in word only is me yelling "I GOT YOU, friend, ANYTHING you need!" and then ducking behind the oven the second forty empty cookie boxes roll in. John says loving in action and truth is how we'll know we belong to the truth.

cards.question: True or false: John says loving in action and truth will also assure our hearts in God's presence.

cards.text: But some days your own heart turns on you and points the finger. John says even if our hearts condemn us, there's something to remember about God.

cards.question: Even if our hearts condemn us, what does John say about God?

answers.text: God is greater than our hearts
God stays far from our hearts

cards.text: And He knows all things. Friend, my heart said a LOT about me back in that junk drawer, none of it nice, and God is greater than every single word of it.

cards.question: True or false: John says if our hearts do not condemn us, we should still be afraid before God.
John says we will receive from Him whatever we ask. Why?

answers.text: We keep His commandments and do what pleases Him
We ask Him again and again until He says yes
We give Him a tenth of everything we earn

cards.text: John just mentioned keeping God's commandments, and now he spells out what His commandment is. It comes in two parts, and part two you already know by heart: love one another.

cards.question: John says part one of His commandment is that we should ___ in the name of His Son, Jesus Christ.

cards.text: John says, "Whoever keeps His commandments remains in God, and God in him." Then he tells us how we can know He remains in us.

cards.question: How does John say we know He remains in us?

answers.text: By the Spirit He has given us
By the signs He shows us each day
By the dreams He gives us at night

findings.problem: The card says John 'says he heard and saw Jesus with his own eyes (1 John 1:1).' 1 John 1:1 says 'we' (not 'he') and speaks of 'the Word of life.' It does not name Jesus. The card changes the speaker from a group to one man and swaps in a name the cited verse doesn't use.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card calls 1 John 'a letter from John,' and every later card says 'John says.' The letter never names its author. The John authorship is church tradition, not something the text states, so no verse can back it up.
findings.question: prep-walkthrough.md allows 'who wrote a letter, with their reference,' but 1 John has no verse naming its author. Can Papa Dorin call the writer John based on tradition (and if so, how should he cite or frame it), or should he call him 'the writer' or 'the apostle' and avoid naming him?

findings.problem: The card says 'loving in action and truth is how we'll know we belong to the truth.' Verse 19 only says 'And by this we will know.' The text doesn't settle whether 'this' points back to verse 18 or ahead to what follows. The card settles that connection as fact.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The true or false statement 'John says loving in action and truth will also assure our hearts in God's presence' is marked True. That answer depends on reading 'by this' in verse 19 as pointing back to verse 18, which the text leaves open. The right answer rests on a connection the text doesn't state.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Stop 2 has only one real laugh (card 3). Story cards 1, 5, 10 and 12 read as plain, pleasant narration, and card 7 is sincere, not funny. Moments like a heart that 'condemns us' (card 5) or the two-part commandment (card 10) could hold a laugh without muddying a fact.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
